posts.body:
New plugin to automate diagonal sprites! New Music! New Graphics!
​
Want to include taller sprites that can walk diagonally but don’t want to spend all your time drawing them yourself? Then you need the Diagonal Sprite Generator! Terunon’s Lab is here with a plugin pack to help turn your existing sprites into taller versions of themselves along with adding diagonal movement. Give Reid a confidence boost by adding a few more inches to his height without stretching his head into a strange new shape, and let the village children run around diagonally instead of sticking to square routes! Simply add the plugin to your project and during the next playtest it will generate sprites based off the current images not marked with a ‘!’ in your character folder. Then you can pick and choose which ones your game needs, and start game making with your shiny new sprites! Plugin parameters let you control the ratio that the body stretches to become taller along with just how large your sprites’ heads are so that their faces don’t accidentally get stretched too.
This pack also includes a plugin to allow for diagonal walking and running movement so that you don’t need to search for another plugin to make use of the generated sprites. The sprite generating plugins work in both MV and MZ, so you can use them to add some diagonal sprites to either engine. If you want to include diagonal sprites but don’t want to take up any of your game dev time doing it by hand, make sure to check out the Diagonal Sprite Generator pack!

Rescue princesses in peril, face off against silly stuffed foes after being shrunk to the size of a toy, race out of a dungeon before time runs out, and more while energetic music plays thanks to the RETRO SOUND MUSIC PACK Vol01! RYUHEIDOU(NISHINO RYUHEI) has created a music pack of 20 BGMs to add some extra pizzazz to your exciting dungeons, emotional cutscenes, and exhilarating battles. Inspired by the soundtracks of 90’s games, this pack is full of nostalgic vibes that will get your players’ toes tapping in no time! Let your heroes battle mobs while ‘Keep Running!’s speedy upbeat tune cheers them on, and warn them of the challenging fight ahead with the frantic and unsettling rhythm of ‘Sword of Darkness’.
Have your heroes share a tender moment where they open up to each other while the relaxing chimes and melody of ‘Sleepy Princess’ plays in the background, and force them to confront feelings they thought they had suppressed when the drumbeats and synth piano of ‘Strange Feeling’ after a shocking fact has been revealed. Or bring a smile to your players with the silly ‘Toy King’ track, where dramatic beats compliment squeaky horns to create a melody that clowns would love. Each track comes in M4a and Ogg file formats so it’s easy to add them to your MV or MZ projects. Pick up RETRO SOUND MUSIC PACK Vol01 and add some excited chiptune tracks and quirky tracks to match your world’s unique locations!

Send a chill down your players’ spines with the Ax Angel Studios - Shattered Silence music pack! Ax Angel Studios joins the music scene with this pack of 14 BGMs inspired by the spooky and scary horror games that appeared at the turn of the century. Have your hero search for safety while heavy bells in the bell tower ring out, make the hairs on the back of their neck stand up when a lonely wind shifts into a haunted piano melody, and get their heart racing when a fast-paced beat lets them know that the monster has spotted them!
Introduce a creepy abandoned mansion while soft piano and clear chimes ring out to warn your players that there’s more to this mansion than rats and forgotten treasures, or skip straight to fear-inducing whines and heavy drums so your players know that a happy ending will be hard to find. Even your non-horror games can use some spooky tracks to help set the scene! Warn your players of potential danger in a factory with uncomfortable clangs and wobbly sheet metal instead of recognizable instruments, or grab the pack’s upbeat track that sounds like it belongs in a Persona game to give your players a reprieve from facing off against all the dangers your game’s world contains.
Each track comes in M4a, MP3, and Ogg file formats so you can use them in your favorite RPG Maker engine. 12 of the tracks also come in fully loopable versions so you can keep the atmosphere going no matter how long it takes your players to work up the courage to finally open that suspicious door. If you need some creepy-crawly tunes to set the mood in a haunted house or just want to add some extra spookiness to a midnight mystery, check out the Ax Angel Studios - Shattered Silence pack!

Fill your 90s-inspired game worlds with hypnotic beats thanks to the Chiptune 8bit BGM Pack! Hefka Games is here with a pack of 30 BGMs made with retro aesthetics and pixel art graphics in mind! Choose from quirky chiptune beeps and boops and mesmerizing melodies to fill your dungeons with upbeat tracks, your battles with heart-pounding tunes, and your villages with uplifting songs to get your players into the right mood!
Give your digital world some fitting electronic sounds with this pack, perfect for creating a world within a world in your modern slice-of-life game for your players to experience in the arcades or use the tracks to lure your players into a false sense of familiarity before springing a mind-bending twist on them. Fill your dungeons with heavy beats to keep your players ready for anything while exploring, and use different tracks during battles to give your players a heads up when a battle may be harder than they expect or give rare monsters their own themes for another reason to battle every chance. Don’t forget to give your players a break from all the excitement with more relaxed and soothing tracks once they’re safe back in a town!
Each track comes in M4a and Ogg file formats so they’re easy to add into your MV and MZ projects, or use them in your favorite RPG Maker engine. If your dungeons could use some new beep and boop-filled tracks or you just want to avoid orchestral tracks in your pixel art game, give the Chiptune 8bit BGM Pack a try!

The "Diagonal Sprite Generator" includes 3 plugins, one of which just increases the height of all the images in the \ img\characters\ folder that didn't have a '!' at the front of the filename when used on its own. The plugin makes  a new folder and put the new, taller versions in it. This plugin doesn't create sprites for diagonal movement on its own. Just had to manually copy the new sprite sheets into the \character\ folder and start a new playtest.
I left the parameters at default. The sprites are a little taller than one tile, which works well with the tilesets I am using. For my tastes, they look a lot better than the default. As I will be doing more with the character generator I will have to do a dummy project to convert the output sheets.
I will do a bit more playtesting, and hopefully, make the taller sprite version the main project.

posts.author: Kenen
posts.body:
This issue regarding whether or not the advertised plugin will or won't generate pixel-perfect sprites is the reason I will not buy resources/DLC from Komodo moving forward and will buy directly from the creator when possible (e.g. via itch).
I understand that the Komodo website has limitations in terms of the image sizes/resolutions that it's configured to display, but the reality is that when the quality of the product you are selling can be measured in pixels, you need to find a way to show your customers the actual pixels, whether they're watermarked, or cropped, or whatever else that needs to be done to protect the assets.

posts.author: Piyan Glupak
posts.body:
@GalacticGod
and
@TheAM-Dol
- Had a quick go, and will put a quick explanation below the images.
Default Size:
Taller Size (not messed with default settings):
The package includes 4 plugins:
TN_DiagonalSpriteGenerator - on its own produces sprite sheets with what I presume are diagonal sprite in default size. If used at the same time as TN_SpriteExtender the new sheets are taller.
TN_SpriteExtenderEx - the only one that I am interested in. On its own it makes the sprites taller.
TN_8DirectionalGenerator - Threw an error when I tried to use it. I don't feel like messing with it.
PD_8DirDash is supposed to do the 8 directional movement. Not tried it out because I have little interest in doing so. I believe that you can use others.
The sprite sheets are generated in new folders. It is up to the user to have a look at them, then what they want into the \img\character\ folder.
If you want my opinion, I am pleased with the normal 4-direction movement taller sprites, but am unsure about the diagonal ones. Luckily for me, I only got the package because I want sprites a little taller than default.
Edit
: I think the forum software  might have made the sheets look the same size. You could try right-clicking on the images and choosing "Open in a new tab".

It might be nice to pick this up this pack to attain the TN_8DirectionalGenerator Plugin so I can generate the actually sprites instead of relying on the Sprite Extender plugin itself.

They mentioned that the SpriteExtenderEx was based upon their previous Sprite Extender plugin that just extended the sprites during the game rather than outputting new sprite sheets. I use Aramis's SpriteZoom to shrink the party on the overworld, so I thought that it would be a good idea to have taller sprite sheets rather than having 2 plugins that resize the sprites during play.
[/QUOTE]
[QUOTE="The_Eerie_One, post: 1437118, member: 256165"]
Would the diagonal generator work with any character sizes and style? Kind of want to use it on the Pop Horror City characters and the Pastel Kawaii Assets character.
[/QUOTE]
If you use TN_SpriteExtenderEX and TN_DiagonalSpriteGenerator plugins together, you get 2 new extra folders, one with taller 4 directional sprites and the other with taller 8 directional sprites.  You have to look at the new sprites sheets and decide whether or you want to copy them into the \img\characters\ folder for your game to use.
[B]TN_SpriteExtenderEX[/B] worked with the sprite sheets that I cobbled-up in the character generator, with the 2 "Big Monster" sheets of MV and the couple of ACE sprite sheets that I tried. In short, it seems to make taller versions of all sprite sheets that I tried.
[B]TN_DiagonalSprite[/B] worked with the 2 ACE sprite sheets I tested ("Riding" and "Spiritual"), and most of the default MV sprites. The ones it had trouble with were the default 2 "Big Monsters" from MV. $BigMonster1 and $BigMonster2 only have 3 frames for each monster, no left, right or rear views, so any results might have come out weird anyway. No idea whether it was the size of the sprites or the fact that every frame on the sheet was front-facing.
